name: Nicoreşti

climate.koppen_name: Cold, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Merlot, Riesling, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon fully without cooking off their freshness.
Merlot sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.
Most rain falls while the vines grow. Damp leaves invite mildew and rot, so growers spray more and pick carefully.

soil.rock: Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water. Sand is warm and airy. It drains fast but holds little water, and phylloxera does not thrive in it. Clay holds water well but drains poorly. It stays cool, which slows ripening and keeps acidity up.
soil.top: The topsoil stores water through dry spells, but stays wet and cold after rain, which slows ripening and can swell the grapes. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: The high ground runs about 2°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Mostly flat. Easy and cheap to farm by machine, but on still nights cold air settles on flat ground, so spring frost is a bigger risk.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
